<think>**Planning prefix encoder helper**

**Implementing direct prefix masks**

**Writing arbiter prefix logic**

**Implementing request-index masking**

</think>

{
  "candidate_rtl": "`resetall
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module arbiter #(
    parameter PORTS = 4,
    parameter ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK_ACK = 1,
    parameter ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [PORTS-1:0] request,
    input wire [PORTS-1:0] acknowledge,
    output wire [PORTS-1:0] grant,
    output wire grant_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded
);

reg [PORTS-1:0] grant_reg, grant_next;
reg grant_valid_reg, grant_valid_next;
reg [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded_reg, grant_encoded_next;
reg [PORTS-1:0] mask_reg, mask_next;

assign grant = grant_reg;
assign grant_valid = grant_valid_reg;
assign grant_encoded = grant_encoded_reg;

wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request = request & mask_reg;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_prefix;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request_prefix;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_winner;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request_winner;
wire request_valid = |request;
wire masked_request_valid = |masked_request;
wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] request_index;
wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] masked_request_index;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_mask;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request_mask;

/* Each prefix says that a higher-priority request exists.  It also
 * directly represents the round-robin mask following this arbitration.
 */
genvar p;
generate
    for (p = 0; p < PORTS; p = p+1) begin : prefix_logic
        if (ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : low_priority_first
            if (p == 0) begin : edge_bit
                assign request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : other_bits
                assign request_prefix[p] = |request[p-1:0];
                assign masked_request_prefix[p] = |masked_request[p-1:0];
            end
        end else begin : high_priority_first
            if (p == PORTS-1) begin : edge_bit
                assign request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_request_prefix[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : other_bits
                assign request_prefix[p] = |request[PORTS-1:p+1];
                assign masked_request_prefix[p] = |masked_request[PORTS-1:p+1];
            end
        end
    end
endgenerate

assign request_winner = request & ~request_prefix;
assign masked_request_winner = masked_request & ~masked_request_prefix;

/* Encode an already one-hot result: there is no priority mux tree here. */
reg [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] request_index_comb;
reg [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] masked_request_index_comb;
integer k;
always @* begin
    request_index_comb = 0;
    masked_request_index_comb = 0;
    for (k = 0; k < PORTS; k = k+1) begin
        request_index_comb = request_index_comb |
            ({$bits(request_index_comb){request_winner[k]}} & k);
        masked_request_index_comb = masked_request_index_comb |
            ({$bits(masked_request_index_comb){masked_request_winner[k]}} & k);
    end
end

/* Preserve the reference encoder's defined outputs even for empty input. */
localparam EMPTY_INDEX = ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY ?
    (PORTS > 2 ? 2**$clog2(PORTS)-1 : 1) : 0;
assign request_index = request_valid ? request_index_comb : EMPTY_INDEX;
assign masked_request_index = masked_request_valid ? masked_request_index_comb : EMPTY_INDEX;
assign request_mask = request_valid ? request_winner : (1 << EMPTY_INDEX);
assign masked_request_mask = masked_request_valid ? masked_request_winner : (1 << EMPTY_INDEX);

always @* begin
    grant_next = 0;
    grant_valid_next = 0;
    grant_encoded_next = 0;
    mask_next = mask_reg;

    if (ARB_BLOCK && !ARB_BLOCK_ACK && (grant_reg & request)) begin
        grant_next = grant_reg;
        grant_valid_next = grant_valid_reg;
        grant_encoded_next = grant_encoded_reg;
    end else if (ARB_BLOCK && ARB_BLOCK_ACK && grant_valid && !(grant_reg & acknowledge)) begin
        grant_next = grant_reg;
        grant_valid_next = grant_valid_reg;
        grant_encoded_next = grant_encoded_reg;
    end else if (request_valid) begin
        grant_valid_next = 1'b1;
        if (ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN) begin
            if (masked_request_valid) begin
                grant_next = masked_request_mask;
                grant_encoded_next = masked_request_index;
                mask_next = masked_request_prefix;
            end else begin
                grant_next = request_mask;
                grant_encoded_next = request_index;
                mask_next = request_prefix;
            end
        end else begin
            grant_next = request_mask;
            grant_encoded_next = request_index;
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin
        grant_reg <= 0;
        grant_valid_reg <= 0;
        grant_encoded_reg <= 0;
        mask_reg <= 0;
    end else begin
        grant_reg <= grant_next;
        grant_valid_reg <= grant_valid_next;
        grant_encoded_reg <= grant_encoded_next;
        mask_reg <= mask_next;
    end
end
endmodule

/* Standalone helper retains the reference interface and parameter behavior. */
module priority_encoder #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4,
    parameter LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] input_unencoded,
    output wire output_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] output_encoded,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] output_unencoded
);
parameter LEVELS = WIDTH > 2 ? $clog2(WIDTH) : 1;
parameter W = 2**LEVELS;
wire [W-1:0] input_padded = {{W-WIDTH{1'b0}}, input_unencoded};
wire [W/2-1:0] stage_valid[LEVELS-1:0];
wire [W/2-1:0] stage_enc[LEVELS-1:0];
generate
    genvar l, n;
    for (n = 0; n < W/2; n = n+1) begin : loop_in
        assign stage_valid[0][n] = |input_padded[n*2+1:n*2];
        if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = !input_padded[n*2];
        end else begin
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = input_padded[n*2+1];
        end
    end
    for (l = 1; l < LEVELS; l = l+1) begin : loop_levels
        for (n = 0; n < W/(2*2**l); n = n+1) begin : loop_compress
            assign stage_valid[l][n] = |stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1:n*2];
            if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2] ?
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]} :
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]};
            end else begin
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1] ?
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]} :
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]};
            end
        end
    end
endgenerate
assign output_valid = stage_valid[LEVELS-1];
assign output_encoded = stage_enc[LEVELS-1];
assign output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded;
endmodule

`resetall
",
  "bottleneck": "The original round-robin datapath priority-encodes requests, decodes the encoded winner into a grant, and constructs the next mask through index arithmetic and a variable shift. These dependent transformations, followed by selection and blocking feedback, are plausible contributors to the measured register-to-register critical paths; the supplied mapped names do not prove exact attribution.",
  "rewrite": "Compute higher-priority-request reductions directly. Each winner bit is its request bit AND the complement of its higher-priority reduction. The same reduction vector is exactly the next round-robin mask, eliminating index-to-mask arithmetic and shifting. Encode the one-hot winners with OR logic only. Keep the original named state registers, synchronous reset, hold conditions, and registered outputs.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to improve setup WNS by removing priority-encode/decode and encode/shift dependencies, especially on mask feedback. No candidate synthesis or STA was available here, so an improvement over the measured 7.79 ns baseline is a prediction, not a verified result.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "No additional registers or latency. Overlapping prefix reductions offer substantial sharing opportunities, while separate masked and unmasked networks retain parallel arbitration. Actual mapped area, the 4855.656960 um2 cap, and electrical limits require evaluation with the specified mapping flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves blocking-on-acknowledge and blocking-on-request behavior, both priority directions, round-robin wraparound, no-request outputs, mask retention, synchronous repeated reset, and existing state encodings. The mask identity holds for every defined request and mask value, not just reachable thermometer masks. No initialization, startup assumption, additional input restriction, or undefined output is introduced. Formal and mapped equivalence still require execution."
}
